paper_title: HeLIOS: The Superfluid Helium Ultralight Dark Matter Detector
notes: This is a prototype demonstration / projection paper. No actual measured exclusion limit is set (attempts to observe thermally driven motion failed). Fig. 1 shows projected sensitivity regions after 1 hr integration for both scalar UDM (d_me, ScalarElectron coupling to electron mass) and vector UDM (g_B-L, VectorBL). The paper constrains BOTH coupling types simultaneously; the hint VectorBL is one of two. Scalar curve is ScalarElectron (d_me, ~1e-7 to 1e7 over masses ~3-50 peV), vector curve is VectorBL (g_B-L ~1e-26 to 1e-16 over ~1-50 peV). No numerical exclusion table or text values for the projection curves are provided; only plot axes ranges. Hence data_points empty and confidence capped at 0.5 due to dual coupling and unreadable plot values. Mass range roughly 4e-12 to 2.3e-10 eV (Compton freq ~1-55 kHz). | Vision: Right panel of Fig.1 shows vector UDM coupling g_BL vs mass [peV]. The lower boundary traced corresponds to the existing experimental bounds (Eot-Wash and LIGO/Virgo) which form the lowest excluded region in the plot. The red HeLIOS projections (and optimized dashed lines) sit higher. Y-axis ticks read from 1e-26 to 1e-16. The provided y-axis calibration (1e-7 to 1e7) does not match the right panel labels which range 1e-26 to 1e-16; I used the actual plotted g_BL values. Values are approximate readings from the log-log plot. | Calibration: No calibration needed
